description.narrative:
In the spring of 2024, Sida began discussions with UN Women about a cost extension of the support that started in 2019. Sida assesses that UN Women has since become a well-functioning and strategic actor and advocate for equality in Sudan. UN Women returned to Sida with a revised needs analysis to identify the need for support for its work in light of the still intense conflict in the country. The now proposed extended support covers needs during the end of 2024 and the years 2025 and 2026.
UN Women proposes to build on the previous work in organizing and strengthening the women's movement in Sudan. This will be done by establishing platforms for female mediators and negotiators, providing opportunities and resources for meaningful participation in peace talks and mediation efforts. Sudanese women's groups will be given the opportunity to participate in peace negotiations and decision-making processes and in Sudan-related regional and global events to build capacity, knowledge and skills in peace processes.
The second identified area is to strengthen preventive work to protect girls and women against gender-based, including sexual, violence. The intervention will not only protect individuals from immediate harm and improve their ability to earn a living, but will contribute to the resilience of communities and lay the foundations for long-term stability and prosperity once conflict has subsided. UN Women has initially identified two states, Gedaref and White Nile, where the organization is already working to increase livelihood opportunities for women and where they already have a built-up network of partners.

Under våren 2024 påbörjade Sida diskussioner med UN Women om en kostnadsförlängning av det stöd som startade 2019. Sida bedömer att UN Women sedan dess blivit en välfungerande och strategisk aktör för jämställhet i Sudan. UN Women återkom till Sida med en reviderad behovsanalys där de identifierade behov av stöd för dess arbete i och med den alltjämt intensiva konflikten i landet. Det nu föreslagna utökade stödet täcker behov under slutet av 2024 samt åren 2025 och 2026.
UN Women föreslår att bygga vidare på det tidigare arbetet med att organisera och stärka kvinnorörelsen i Sudan. Detta kommer att ske genom att etablera plattformar för kvinnliga medlare och förhandlare, vilket ger möjligheter och resurser för meningsfullt deltagande i fredssamtal och medlingsinsatser. Sudanesiska kvinnogrupper kommer ges möjlighet att delta i fredsförhandlingar och beslutsprocesser och i Sudan-relaterade regionala och globala evenemang för att bygga kapacitet, kunskap och färdigheter i fredsprocesser.
Det andra identifierade området är att stärka det förebyggande arbete för att skydda flickor och kvinnor mot könsrelaterat, inklusive sexuell våld. Insatsen kommer inte bara att skydda individer från omedelbar skada och förbättra deras förmåga att skaffa försörjning, utan kommer att bidra till samhällenas motståndskraft och lägga grunden för långsiktig stabilitet och välstånd när konflikten har lagt sig. UN Women har initialt identifierat två delstater, Gedaref and White Nile, där organisationen redan arbetar för att öka försörjningsmöjligheter för kvinnor och där de redan har ett uppbyggt nätverk av samarbetspartner.

Women influencing the course of peace in Sudan: A leadership and economic empowerment nexus
The objective has been changed during the programme phase. The objectives and results below relates to the amendment that is currently underway. The objectives reflects the needs as assessed since the way broke out.
Outcome 1: A more inclusive, coordinated, and sustainable women movement grounded in nexus of feminism, peace and humanitarianism influences regional and International political/peace processes
Output 1.1: Enhanced institutional capacity of womens organizations (civic and political) through strengthen womens leadership, skills, capacity, and knowledge on peace related issues at local, regional, and national levels.
Output 1.2: Established platforms for women mediators, negotiators, providing opportunities/resources for their meaningful participation in peace talks and mediation efforts.
Output 1.3: Increased inclusive dialogues, forums and engagement that amplify womens voices facilitating their participation in peace process.
Outcome 2: Strengthened Community Response to GBV, Communities in Sudan in Gedaref and White Nile states will be better equipped with knowledge and resources to effectively to prevent and respond to gender-based violence (GBV), fostering safer environments and promoting resilience and peace
Output 2.1: Create a conducive environment for GBV survivors to come forward for support thereby also increasing the use of GBV referral systems made available by UNFPA.
Output 2.2: Women, girls, men and communities are better informed about GBV, women rights and have access to livelihood opportunities.
Output 2.3: Local communities, young males, male community leaders and aid field workers better sensitized on the issues around GBV, focusing on human rights, the criminal aspects of GBV and potential judicial consequences

description.narrative:
Summary of main results (Outcome 1)
Strengthened women's collective leadership and coordination. The Peace for Sudan Platform expanded from 43 to 50 organizations, evolving into a coordinated advocacy coalition with shared positions and joint representation in national, regional and international forums.
More than 50 women strengthened their skills in leadership, mediation, negotiation and advocacy, creating a network of trained women peacebuilders better equipped to engage in peace and humanitarian processes.
Women's organizations agreed on common priorities, including women's participation in peace processes, accountability for conflict-related sexual violence, humanitarian access and direct funding for women-led organizations which were consistently promoted across nine international advocacy platforms.
Two national coordination platforms were established on women's access to justice and UNSCR 1325 and political participation - strengthening collaboration among women's organizations.
Sudanese women engaged directly with the UN Country Team, African Union, UN Special Envoy and other international actors, resulting in commitments from UN partners to strengthen engagement with women-led organizations and increase support for their participation in humanitarian and peace processes.
Overall, the programme strengthened the institutional foundations for women's meaningful participation in future peace processes by improving coordination, leadership, advocacy and access to decision-makers, despite the continued exclusion of women from formal peace negotiations.
Summary of main results (Outcome 2)
The programme supported the set up three Comprehensive Women and Girls Safe Spaces (CWGSS), community referral mechanisms and coordination systems, creating the foundation for survivor-centred GBV services in Gedaref and White Nile States.
During the first implementation period, 1 613 people (1 496 women and 117 men) benefited from GBV prevention, psychosocial support, referral and livelihoods activities, while 66 GBV survivors were identified and referred to specialized case management.
The programme strengthened community awareness and resilience. GBV awareness and women's rights activities reached 752 community members, exceeding the annual target, while 50 women completed livelihoods training and the first Village Savings and Loan Association (VSLA) was established to strengthen women's economic resilience.
The programme trained 20 community leaders on survivor-centred referral pathways and protection principles, laying the groundwork for stronger community-based GBV prevention and response.
Although dignity kit distribution and community peace dialogues were delayed by procurement and administrative processes, the programme reports that it established the systems, partnerships and referral structures needed to scale up GBV prevention and response in subsequent phases.
Overall, the programme achieved start-up and systems-building results, improving access to survivor-centred services and community-based protection, while recognising that longer-term changes in GBV prevention, help-seeking behaviour and community norms have not yet been demonstrated.
